clue.text: Used to get rebellious when put out

indicators.note: letters that get rebellious refuse to stay in line, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's old habits turn mutinous once they are pushed aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get rebellious' rearranges the six letters of USED TO; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ousted is to be expelled or removed, just as someone put out has been ejected.

clue.text: Subdued, so possibly move with care

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone, having calmed down, may move about cautiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges MOVE and CARE together; 'with' only joins them, and 'so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcame is the past tense of overcome, meaning defeated or conquered.

parts.note: sub- means below or inferior, as in subordinate
a stance is a way of standing

explanation.surface: Low status turns out to be what really matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Substance is physical matter, the stuff something is made of.

parts.note: a toxophilite is an archer; the circus is not a big top but Piccadilly Circus, whose statue shows a winged archer

explanation.surface: A bow-wielding performer under the big top.
explanation.walkthrough: The statue at Piccadilly Circus in London, popularly named for the Greek god of love, shows a winged boy with a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: The god of love shoots arrows, and his statue stands in London's Piccadilly Circus, making him an archer of that circus.

explanation.surface: Something is described as precise but no cure-all.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific is a remedy aimed at one particular ailment rather than a universal cure; as an adjective it means precise or explicit.

clue.text: The shade a friend holds painters love

indicators.note: holds means the first piece contains the others

parts.note: a pal is a friend
RAs are Royal Academicians, painters
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A friend has artists who adore the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: An RA is a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts, so 'painters' are RAs; 'holds' signals the container, and 'The shade' is the sunshade itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a light umbrella giving protection from the sun.

clue.text: Old driver seeing a fight in comfort

indicators.note: in means the first pieces sit inside the comfort word

parts.note: to cheer is to comfort
a riot is a violent disturbance or fight

explanation.surface: A veteran motorist watches a brawl from an armchair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old driver' suggests an elderly motorist; it is the driver of an ancient chariot. 'in' signals the container and 'seeing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A charioteer drove a chariot in ancient times, so is a driver of long ago.

indicators.note: almost means one letter short of the full phrase

parts.note: if you tripped over something you fell on it

explanation.surface: A criminal nearly stumbled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops one L from FELL ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A felon is a criminal, someone who has committed a serious crime.

parts.note: a cut is a reduction, as in a price cut
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A permitted cut in the meat ration.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlet is a small piece of meat, typically a chop from the neck.

clue.text: Making fools do it is wrong

indicators.note: is wrong signals that the letters are out of their correct order

explanation.surface: A moral statement that it is wrong to make fools of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is wrong' rearranges DO IT IS; 'Making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiots are stupid people, the same as fools.

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned exclamation about needlework as a household chore.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroider is to decorate cloth with needlework, once thought of as women's work, and also to embellish a story with fanciful details.

indicators.note: after places the turned word behind the other piece in the answer

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back tells us the little word to is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: Instructions in a card game about dealing again once everyone has had a go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' is a verb here, not a noun about a bargain; 'back' reverses the short word and 'after' places it at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal out and to allot both mean to distribute shares among people.

parts.note: to score a surface is to cut a line into it
E is east, one of the compass points

explanation.surface: Winning a point in debate shows how sharp someone is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' looks like a sporting term but means to incise, CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute can mean shrewd or sharp-witted, as in a cute move by a canny operator.

parts.note: to con is an old word for studying or learning by heart
a science can mean a skill or technique, as in the science of boxing

explanation.surface: The theory underlying a method of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscience is a person's moral sense, the inner principles that guide right and wrong.

parts.note: a lamp used when everything is under water, from a deluge, gives the question mark its punning reading

explanation.surface: A question about lighting a submerged scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual sense is a powerful lamp lighting a building or stadium; the clue reads it as light during an inundation.
explanation.definitionFit: A powerful lamp that bathes an area in light is read as the light of a deluge, because a flood leaves everything under water.

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong for these words, so their letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone notes with regret that the men's cover is the final one in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges MEN LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantle is a cloak or layer, so mantles as a verb means envelops or cloaks.

explanation.surface: A question about straw put down for a household's pets.
explanation.definitionFit: Litter is straw used as bedding for animals, and a litter is a brood of young born to one animal at once.

clue.text: Cut up over pit workers, they seek satisfactory answers

indicators.note: over places the first piece above the second in this down answer
in a down clue, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: to axe is to cut
miners work in coal pits

explanation.surface: Cutbacks affect coal miners who are demanding proper answers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AXE into EXA, and 'over' places it above MINERS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Examiners set and mark tests, looking for correct responses from candidates.

clue.text: He'll argue about a certain issue with little hesitation

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a certain one, any single one, gives the article a
a son is issue, an offspring
er is the short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone will debate a definite question with barely a pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a matter for debate, but it means offspring, SON.
explanation.definitionFit: A reasoner is someone who thinks logically and argues a case.

clue.text: Letter about a cat taken back and put down

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: DEE is the spelt-out name of the letter D

indicators.note: taken back means the word for the cat is written in reverse

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A letter mentioning a pet returned to its owner before it was put to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' is not a written message but the name of a letter of the alphabet spelt out; 'taken back' reverses the cat and 'about' wraps the letter round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone down a rank is to demote them, lowering their status.

parts.note: falling short of any finish describes something that never stops

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles before getting to the end of an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Falling'; read it as falling short of a finish, describing something without an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something interminable goes on and on, never arriving at any final point.

clue.text: Quietly agrees maybe to make a prediction

parts.note: P is piano, the musical instruction to play quietly

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word agrees could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken nod of assent leading to a forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' signals the anagram of the word after 'Quietly'; 'to' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To presage is to foretell or portend what is coming.

explanation.surface: Someone having a drink at the station.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a description of a person: the one found at the railway station carrying bags.
explanation.definitionFit: Porter is a dark beer, and a porter carries luggage for travellers at a station.

clue.text: A mean head of state causes humiliation

parts.note: base means mean or low

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A stingy head of state is a cause of national embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like an adjective about character, but it is BASE; 'head of' takes S from 'state'.
explanation.definitionFit: To abase someone is to humble or degrade them, which brings them shame.

clue.text: The struggle to serve again is a racket!

parts.note: a battle is a struggle or fight
to do is to serve or suffice, as in that will do
re- is the prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: A tennis player complains that having to serve once more is a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' looks like an outburst of protest; it is the bat used in battledore and shuttlecock, the forerunner of badminton.
explanation.definitionFit: A battledore is a small racquet used to hit a shuttlecock in the old game of that name.

clue.text: A flash — a little electric energy discharge

indicators.note: a little of these words means only a part of the run is taken

explanation.surface: A brief spark of static electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' takes TRICE from 'elecTRIC Energy'; 'discharge' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A trice is an instant, the time it takes for a flash.

explanation.surface: A question about whether jumping about is girlish.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss something is to skip or pass it over, and a miss is a girl or unmarried young woman.

clue.text: Monster climbing pass followed by soldiers

indicators.note: followed by puts the soldiers after the first piece
in a down answer, climbing means the word is read upwards

parts.note: to go is to pass, as when a player passes a turn
RE is the Royal Engineers, a regiment of soldiers

explanation.surface: A monster climbs a mountain pass with troops behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns GO into OG in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore.

clue.text: Carol is about 50 and so shy …

indicators.note: is about means the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: to carol is to sing joyfully
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A woman named Carol, nearing fifty, is described as bashful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name but is a verb, SING; 'is about' wraps it round L.
explanation.definitionFit: To shy is to throw or fling, and to sling means the same.

parts.note: ever means always or perpetually
green describes someone inexperienced or naive

explanation.surface: Continuing a story about women: Olive, it seems, is forever innocent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olive' looks like a woman's name continuing the run from Carol, but it is the tree, which keeps its leaves all year.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive tree keeps its leaves through winter, so it is an example of a plant that never sheds foliage.

clue.text: … she is wet perhaps but rather nice

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words she is wet may be rearranged

explanation.surface: The third woman in the series may be feeble, but she is pleasant enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges SHE IS WET; the dots continue the story of Carol and Olive.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetish means somewhat pleasant, the -ish ending softening the adjective as 'rather' does.

parts.note: lesser or less means minor or smaller
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A landlord handing over a small amount of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessor is the party who grants a lease, a landlord letting out property.
